scenes.tts: If the Hox code sets a segment's identity, what happens when one gene is taken away?
scenes.visual: Title card: Remove One Letter. The hindbrain code grid with the Hoxb1 row flickering out.
scenes.narration: If the Hox code sets a segment's identity, what happens when one gene is taken away?

scenes.tts: A conventional knockout is a mouse line with one gene disrupted in every cell.
scenes.visual: A mouse outline; every cell shows one gene crossed out. Label: conventional knockout.
scenes.narration: A conventional knockout is a mouse line with one gene disrupted in every cell.

scenes.tts: In a normal mouse, facial motor neurons are born in r four and migrate back to r six. There they form the facial motor nucleus.
scenes.caption: In a normal mouse, facial motor neurons are born in r4 and migrate back to r6. There they form the facial motor nucleus.
scenes.visual: Normal mouse hindbrain: neurons appear in r4 and stream back to r6, where they cluster, labelled facial motor nucleus; nerve VII runs to a face outline.
scenes.narration: In a normal mouse, facial motor neurons are born in r4 and migrate back to r6. There they form the facial motor nucleus.

scenes.tts: In the Hox code, Hox B one is the clearest difference between r four and r three.
scenes.caption: In the Hox code, Hoxb1 is the clearest difference between r4 and r3.
scenes.visual: Grid columns r3 and r4; Hoxa2 and Hoxb2 glow in both, and the strong Hoxb1 dot in r4 lights up. Label: simplified table.
scenes.narration: In the Hox code, Hoxb1 is the clearest difference between r4 and r3.

scenes.tts: Predict. Knock out Hox B one. Does r four disappear? Or does it stay and become something else?
scenes.caption: Predict. Knock out Hoxb1. Does r4 disappear? Or does it stay and become something else?
scenes.visual: Question card: knock out Hoxb1. Does r4 disappear, or stay and change?
scenes.narration: Predict. Knock out Hoxb1. Does r4 disappear? Or does it stay and become something else?

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, two groups reported Hox B one knockouts. One was led by Studer and Krumlauf, the other by Goddard and Capecchi.
scenes.caption: In 1996, two groups reported Hoxb1 knockouts. One was led by Studer and Krumlauf, the other by Goddard and Capecchi.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Studer and Krumlauf; Goddard and Capecchi; 1996, mouse.
scenes.narration: In 1996, two groups reported Hoxb1 knockouts. One was led by Studer and Krumlauf, the other by Goddard and Capecchi.

scenes.tts: Rhombomere four was still there. Its progenitors still divided, and still made motor neurons.
scenes.visual: Mutant hindbrain: the r4 outline stays in place, with dividing progenitors and new neurons inside it.
scenes.narration: Rhombomere four was still there. Its progenitors still divided, and still made motor neurons.

scenes.tts: But r four lost parts of its identity. Its motor neurons behaved like the trigeminal neurons of r two and r three.
scenes.caption: But r4 lost parts of its identity. Its motor neurons behaved like the trigeminal neurons of r2 and r3.
scenes.visual: The r4 neurons take on the trigeminal colour of r2 and r3.
scenes.narration: But r4 lost parts of its identity. Its motor neurons behaved like the trigeminal neurons of r2 and r3.

scenes.tts: In both mutants, the facial motor neurons failed to form or to migrate normally. No normal facial motor nucleus formed.
scenes.visual: The stream from r4 to r6 stalls; the r6 cluster labelled facial motor nucleus stays empty.
scenes.narration: In both mutants, the facial motor neurons failed to form or to migrate normally. No normal facial motor nucleus formed.

scenes.tts: Compare a different gene, Krox twenty. Without it, r three and r five do not persist as distinct segments. Some of their cells survive, mix with neighbours, and take on their character. In kreisler mutants, r five is missing.
scenes.caption: Compare a different gene, Krox20. Without it, r3 and r5 do not persist as distinct segments. Some of their cells survive, mix with neighbours, and take on their character. In kreisler (MafB) mutants, r5 is missing.
scenes.visual: Right: a continuous Krox20 mutant hindbrain in which the distinct r3 and r5 territories fade out. A few lineage-labelled cells remain where r3 and r5 were and recolour to match their even-numbered neighbours. Below: kreisler (MafB) mutant row with r5 missing.
scenes.narration: Compare a different gene, Krox20. Without it, r3 and r5 do not persist as distinct segments. Some of their cells survive, mix with neighbours, and take on their character. In kreisler (MafB) mutants, r5 is missing.

scenes.tts: So there are two different outcomes. Without Krox twenty, distinct territories are lost. Without Hox B one, r four remains but changes.
scenes.caption: So there are two different outcomes. Without Krox20, distinct territories are lost. Without Hoxb1, r4 remains but changes.
scenes.visual: Two labels: territory lost (cells survive, mix, change identity) beside the Krox20 row; identity changed, segment kept beside the Hoxb1 row. Note: territory and identity are coupled.
scenes.narration: So there are two different outcomes. Without Krox20, distinct territories are lost. Without Hoxb1, r4 remains but changes.

scenes.tts: That is the code acting as a cause, not just a marker.
scenes.visual: Card: two mutants, two outcomes. Krox20 lost: distinct territory lost. Hoxb1 lost: segment kept, identity changed. Below: cause, not just marker.
scenes.narration: That is the code acting as a cause, not just a marker.

scenes.tts: Next: where do the code's edges come from?
scenes.visual: The grid again, with each domain's front edge pulsing.
scenes.narration: Next: where do the code's edges come from?

scenes.tts: The takeaway: without Hox B one, r four survives but loses key parts of its identity. Other Hox knockouts differ, gene by gene.
scenes.visual: Closing card: lose Hoxb1, keep r4, change its identity. Small print: other Hox genes, other outcomes.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: without Hoxb1, r4 survives but loses key parts of its identity. Other Hox knockouts differ, gene by gene.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: without Hoxb1, r4 survives but loses key parts of its identity. Other Hox knockouts differ, gene by gene.
